otherReports.title: Nickel Market: Rally, Correction and the Outlook for Supply Rebalancing
otherReports.summary: Nickel prices recovered 30% in H1 2026 on Indonesian supply cuts and sulfur disruptions, but corrected amid high inventories.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Nickel prices surged ~30% from 2025 lows due to Indonesian mining quota cuts of 25-34% and sulfur supply disruptions affecting HPAL refining costs.
  • Indonesian government reduced 2026 mining quotas from 375-379 million WMT to 250-270 million WMT, signaling shift toward supply discipline.
  • Sulfur shortages from Middle East geopolitical tensions added ~$4,000/tonne to HPAL production costs, with spot prices doubling to $1,000/tonne.
  • Global nickel market transitioning from surplus to potential deficit in 2026, per International Nickel Study Group forecasts.
  • Despite supply tightening, LME and SHFE inventories reached highest levels since 2015, delaying price rebalancing.
  • Medium-term price targets: MCX Nickel ₹2,020 and LME nickel $21,250/tonne supported by structural supply constraints.

otherReports.summary: Precious metals declined as geopolitical support was offset by stronger dollar and Treasury yields.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Gold traded under pressure as geopolitical support was offset by stronger dollar and Treasury yields.

  • Markets reduced geopolitical premium as ceasefire headlines and diplomatic negotiations resurfaced.
  • US headline inflation remained influenced by energy prices, while core inflation showed signs of easing.
  • Fed maintained slightly hawkish stance, citing persistent inflation risks.

otherReports.summary: Copper prices fell 7% in June on macro headwinds and hawkish Fed, with tariff uncertainty persisting.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Copper briefly rallied above $14,000/t in early June amid US tariff speculation.
  • Prices closed 7% lower in June on macroeconomic headwinds and hawkish Fed.
  • US considering 15% tariff on refined copper from January 2027, increasing to 30% in 2028.

  • COMEX inventories increased to 650,412 tonnes, up 5% MoM and 26% YTD.
  • LME inventories declined to 349,225 tonnes, down 12% MoM but 98% above year-start.

otherReports.title: Base Metals- Aluminium
otherReports.summary: Aluminium prices collapsed 14% in June as geopolitical tensions eased and dollar strengthened.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Aluminium prices fell 14% in June after rallying for months, retreating on eased Middle East tensions and stronger US dollar.
  • LME Cash-3M shifted from historic premium into discount, reflecting easing supply concerns.
  • LME inventories declined to 313,800 tonnes, down 10% MoM and 41% YTD, at multi-year lows.
  • SHFE inventories increased to 528,885 tonnes, up 0.5% MoM and 300% YTD, reflecting domestic oversupply.
  • US tariffs and Europe's CBAM continue to distort regional trade flows.
  • Rotterdam premiums eased to $567.5/t, remaining 65% higher YTD.

otherReports.title: Base Metals- Zinc
otherReports.summary: Zinc prices remained resilient in June as supply constraints outweighed weak industrial demand.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Zinc prices resilient as supply constraints outweighed weak industrial demand.
  • Global mine output increased following restart of Tara, Kipushi, and Ozernoye mines.
  • Refined zinc supply remained tight due to production cuts and smelter disruptions ex-China.
  • Tight Western supply and ample Chinese availability supported LME zinc prices.
  • LME inventories rose 18% MoM to 123,450 tonnes; SHFE stocks increased 8% MoM to 156,797 tonnes.

otherReports.title: Precious Metals Weekly : Gold Climbs Above $4,100 Amid Easing Geopolitical Tensions
otherReports.summary: Gold gained as Middle East tensions eased slightly, though dollar strength and high Treasury yields limited further upside momentum.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Gold started the week with strong gains, climbing above $4,100 amid signs of easing geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East.
  • Renewed military tensions involving US, Iran and Yemen's Houthi rebels continued to dent bullion demand for three consecutive weeks.
  • Stronger U.S. dollar, elevated Treasury yields above 4.70%, and inflation concerns limited gold's upside momentum.
  • President Trump announced temporary pause in military operations against Iran, improving sentiment and supporting diplomatic efforts.
  • Global gold-backed ETFs recorded net inflows as investors increased safe-haven allocations amid geopolitical uncertainty.
  • MCX Gold closed at ₹143,106 with support at ₹139,800 and resistance at ₹146,000; buying on dips recommended.

otherReports.title: Zinc: A Measured Climb Amid Tight Fundamentals
otherReports.summary: Zinc prices gained over 30% year-on-year in 2026 due to persistent supply disruptions and low exchange inventories despite recovering mine production.
otherReports.bulletSummary:
• Zinc prices surged more than 30% year-on-year in 2026, defying expectations of a global surplus due to supply disruptions and resilient demand.
  • LME warehouse inventories declined by nearly 24,000 tonnes since late June to around 100,000 tonnes, while SHFE inventories remain near 120,000 tonnes.
  • Major mine projects including Huoshaoyan in China, Bunker Hill in the US, and McIlvenna Bay in Canada are adding capacity but recovery remains slower than anticipated.
  • Global refined zinc demand is expected to grow by approximately 1% in 2026, supported by infrastructure investment offsetting weakness in China's property sector.
  • ILZSG revised its 2026 forecast from surplus to a small deficit of around 19,000 tonnes due to slower supply growth and operational disruptions.
  • Zinc prices are expected to remain supported above $3,500/tonne on LME and ₹360 on MCX, with potential to test $4,000/tonne and ₹410 respectively.
